facts.text: Redmond sits in a fertile basin carved by ancient glaciers, a landscape that once supported thousands of salmon and gave the town its original name, Salmonberg.
The first European settlers arrived in the 1870s, with Luke McRedmond filing a Homestead Act claim in 1870 and Warren Perrigo following in 1871.
In 1889, the Seattle, Lake Shore and Eastern Railway built a station in downtown Redmond, sparking a boom in logging and turning the town into a regional hub.
Redmond’s library, the second‑largest branch in the King County Library System, opened in 1947 after the city joined the county system.
Today, Redmond is best known as the headquarters of Microsoft and Nintendo of America, two tech giants that employ tens of thousands of people in the city.
